title: Harper et al. 2021. How does hormone transition in transgender women change body composition, muscle strength and haemoglobin? Systematic review (Br J Sports Med)
why: Anchor systematic review: haemoglobin, lean mass, strength timelines on feminising HRT

title: Harper et al. 2025. Longitudinal Performance Changes in Transgender Women Athletes Pre and Post Gender Affirming Hormone Therapy (Eur J Sport Sci)
why: Only longitudinal athlete performance dataset; training volume predicted retained performance

title: Hilton & Lundberg 2021. Transgender Women in the Female Category of Sport: Perspectives on Testosterone Suppression and Performance Advantage (Sports Med)
why: Most-cited critical review of retained lean mass and strength after suppression

title: Hamilton et al. 2024. Strength, power and aerobic capacity of transgender athletes: a cross-sectional study (Br J Sports Med)
why: Direct athlete measurement of strength, power, aerobic capacity; supplies most citation hops

title: Coleman et al. 2022. Standards of Care for the Health of Transgender and Gender Diverse People, Version 8 (Int J Transgend Health)
why: WPATH SOC8: hormone, surgical and post-operative activity guidance; open full text

title: Roberts et al. 2020. Effect of gender affirming hormones on athletic performance in transwomen and transmen (Br J Sports Med)
why: USAF longitudinal fitness-test cohort; run, push-up, sit-up change over HRT

title: Wiik et al. 2020. Muscle Strength, Size, and Composition Following 12 Months of Gender-affirming Treatment in Transgender Individuals (J Clin Endocrinol Metab)
why: Only 12-month imaging plus strength study; strength held while thigh volume fell

title: Gois et al. 2025. Body mass index and body composition changes in transgender people undergoing gender-affirming hormone therapy: systematic review and meta-analysis (Rev Endocr Metab Disord)
why: Newest pooled body-composition effect sizes for lean mass and fat mass

title: Hembree et al. 2017. Endocrine Treatment of Gender-Dysphoric/Gender-Incongruent Persons: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline (J Clin Endocrinol Metab)
why: Reference regimens, monitoring intervals and effect-timeline tables; tables render free

title: Peitzmeier et al. 2017. Health impact of chest binding among transgender adults: a community-engaged, cross-sectional study (Cult Health Sex)
why: Only large binding-harm dataset; underpins all exercise-and-binding guidance

title: International Powerlifting Federation. IPF Policy Statement for Transgender Athletes, v3, 21 August 2023 (PDF)
why: IPF policy text: testosterone below 2.4 nmol/L, declaration and passport rules

title: World Athletics. Book C, Regulation C3.5A, Eligibility Regulations for Transgender Athletes, effective 31 March 2023 (PDF)
why: Operative World Athletics regulation text rather than the press summary

title: World Aquatics. Policy on Eligibility for the Men's and Women's Competition Categories, version 24 March 2023 (PDF)
why: Current World Aquatics policy text superseding the June 2022 FINA version

title: Union Cycliste Internationale. The UCI adapts its rules on the participation of transgender athletes in international competitions, 14 July 2023
why: UCI rule change announcement, effective 17 July 2023, with stated rationale

title: NCAA. Participation Policy for Transgender Student-Athletes, effective 6 February 2025
why: Current US collegiate rule; practice-versus-competition distinction matters for client planning

title: Klaver et al. 2018. Changes in regional body fat, lean body mass and body shape in trans persons using cross-sex hormonal therapy (Eur J Endocrinol)
why: Source of the regional fat redistribution and hip circumference numbers

title: Alvares et al. 2022. Cardiopulmonary capacity and muscle strength in transgender women on long-term gender-affirming hormone therapy (Br J Sports Med)
why: Long-term HRT cohort with VO2 and strength measures; Hamilton reference 41

title: Getahun et al. 2018. Cross-sex Hormones and Acute Cardiovascular Events in Transgender Persons: A Cohort Study (Ann Intern Med)
why: Underlies the VTE and stroke referral triggers; open full text

title: Wiepjes et al. 2019. Bone Safety During the First Ten Years of Gender-Affirming Hormonal Treatment in Transwomen and Transmen (J Bone Miner Res)
why: Ten-year bone and fracture outcomes behind the load-anyway recommendation

title: Wiepjes et al. 2017. Bone Mineral Density Increases in Trans Persons After 1 Year of Hormonal Treatment (J Bone Miner Res)
why: Source of the year-one lumbar spine and total hip BMD figures

title: Khan et al. 2019. Venous Thrombotic Risk in Transgender Women Undergoing Estrogen Therapy: A Systematic Review and Metaanalysis (Clin Chem)
why: Pooled VTE incidence per 1000 person-years quoted in the safety section

title: Angus et al. 2019. Cyproterone acetate or spironolactone in lowering testosterone concentrations for transgender individuals receiving oestradiol therapy (Endocr Connect)
why: Antiandrogen choice and testosterone suppression; explains spironolactone side-effect referral triggers

title: Lightner et al. 2024. Physical activity among transgender individuals: a systematic review of quantitative and qualitative studies (PLoS One)
why: Systematic review of gym access, safety and body-image barriers to physical activity

title: Teti et al. 2020. Physical activity and body image: intertwined health priorities identified by transmasculine young people (Int J Transgend Health)
why: Evidence for restricted eating and exercise-avoidance risk in transmasculine clients

title: Lundberg et al. 2024. The IOC framework on fairness, inclusion and nondiscrimination does not protect fairness for female athletes (Scand J Med Sci Sports)
why: Peer-reviewed record of the IOC 2021 framework text; IOC site unfetchable

title: Lundberg & Hilton 2024. Authors' Reply to Hamilton et al. on testosterone suppression and performance advantage (Sports Med)
why: Documents the live methodological dispute between the two primary review camps

title: Deutsch (ed.) 2016. Guidelines for the Primary and Gender-Affirming Care of Transgender and Gender Nonbinary People, 2nd edition (UCSF)
why: Source of sex-specific reference-range guidance for reading client lab values
